title: Deep learning finds an ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death
summary: The Nature paper, published online on 2026-06-24, reports a deep-learning ECG biomarker evaluated retrospectively in Swedish data and external US and Taiwanese datasets. Its high-risk group comprised 2.2% of the sample and had a 7.0% annual sudden-cardiac-death rate, versus 4.6% for reduced LVEF; 86.1% were not flagged by LVEF. Among high-risk patients with defibrillators, sudden cardiac death was 54.4% lower than model-expected, an observational association subject to confounding and not proof of benefit.
ai_technology: Deep learning ECG model with a generative ECG waveform model for visualization
organization: University of California, Berkeley; University of Chicago; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Halmstad University; Region Halland; University of Gothenburg; Sahlgrenska University Hospital

evidence.tested: Existing Swedish ECG/death-certificate data, a held-out lockbox created before analysis, external US ventricular-arrhythmia and Taiwanese arrhythmic-arrest evaluations; observational defibrillator associations.
evidence.unknown: Main paper reviewed; supplementary attachments not read. The authors explicitly identify residual confounding and the need for randomized testing of defibrillator benefit in model-high-risk patients.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model discovered the predictive ECG waveform pattern; generative model used to visualize it.
